newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says to pick delegation to discuss HK links.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says to pick delegation to discuss HK links.

text.p: Taiwan said on Thursday it would send a "parallel" delegation to Hong Kong to discuss shipping links between the two sides after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule from July 1.

Transportation minister Tsai Chao-yang said his ministry would act quickly to select a delegation following China's recent decision to authorise a private Hong Kong association to negotiate the issue.

"We will get together in the near future with the Mainland Affairs Council (Taiwan's top policy-making body on China) to determine a parallel unit to negotiate the issue with Hong Kong," Tsai told parliamentary legislators.

The council said a semi-official body under its wing had received a letter from its Chinese counterpart on Wednesday notifying them that Beijing had authorised the Hong Kong Shipowners' Association to undertake shipping talks.

But the council did not give a timetable for the meeting, and declined to say if Taiwan's ban on direct official contacts with China would prevent council officials from participating in the negotiations with Hong Kong.
"We have not made a final decision, but we will consider everything," council vice-chairman Lin Chung-bin told reporters.
Taiwan businessmen have urged their government to secure direct shipping links with Hong Kong, which reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years as a British colony.
Taiwan, estranged from the mainland after the Chinese civil war ended in 1949, bans direct travel to and from China.

Hong Kong is an important transit point for the more than US$30 billion in investments that have poured into China from Taiwan since the easing of unofficials ties between Beijing and Taipei in the late 1980s.
So far, Taipei and Beijing have remained divided on how direct shipping should work due to basic sovereignty issues.
